summary: Added path-traversal guard inside the workspace-iteration loop of addRepositoryToProject() in repository-orchestrator.ts.

Guard computes resolvedProjectsFolder = path.resolve(config.projectsFolder) once before the Promise.all, then per workspace resolves the destination and checks startsWith(resolvedProjectsFolder + path.sep).
Throws Error with message containing 'Security check failed' if the resolved clone path escapes projectsFolder.
Guard is applied per-workspace (inside the async map callback), consistent with the per-workspace guard pattern in removeRepositoryFromProject().

Added 1 new integration test: 'addRepositoryToProject rejects a clone path that resolves outside projectsFolder'. Test injects a traversal repo ID (../../../../escape) directly into repositories.json to bypass public-API validators, then asserts addRepositoryToProject() throws /Security check failed/.
All 344 tests pass (npm test exit code 0).

comments.note: repository-orchestrator.ts: resolvedProjectsFolder is now computed in two separate methods (addRepositoryToProject and removeRepositoryFromProject). A small private helper like resolvedProjectsFolder() would eliminate the duplication, though it's minor at 1 line each.

addRepositoryToProject() mutates project data (via projectManager.addRepository) before the per-workspace clone loop runs. If the path-traversal guard fires, the project data record is already updated but no clone occurred — this leaves the data model inconsistent with the filesystem. The existing JSDoc says 'The project data update is not rolled back on clone failure', but the path-traversal case is a security rejection, not a soft failure. Consider either moving the guard before the data mutation or adding explicit rollback for the security-check path.

removeRepositoryFromProject() appends a trailing period to the 'Security check failed' message (e.g. '...projectsFolder "...".') while the newly added guard in addRepositoryToProject() does not. Both messages should be consistent. Suggest harmonizing by adding the trailing period to the new guard's message.

summary: Reviewed 2 files (repository-orchestrator.ts, repository-orchestrator.test.ts). OWASP Top 10 full review completed. 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 2 Medium observations (post-mutation guard ordering; path disclosure in error messages) and 1 Low observation (no audit logging of traversal attempts) recorded. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A01/A04 — No Critical/High access-control bypass. The path-traversal guard in addRepositoryToProject() (lines 109-115, repository-orchestrator.ts) correctly uses path.resolve() + startsWith(resolvedProjectsFolder + path.sep) per workspace, mirroring the guard in removeRepositoryFromProject(). All OWASP A01 vectors (path traversal, privilege escalation, IDOR) are addressed by the guard.

A04 — Insecure Design (Medium): repository-orchestrator.ts line 97 — projectManager.addRepository() mutates the project data store before the per-workspace clone loop runs (lines 104-132). If the path-traversal guard fires (lines 110-115), the repository is already recorded in the project's Repositories list but no clone exists. The security control prevents the unsafe filesystem operation, so no access-control bypass occurs; however, the guard firing after the side effect leaves the data model inconsistent with the filesystem. Remediation: pre-compute the resolved destination paths and run all guard checks before line 97 (prior to data mutation), or add explicit rollback on security-check failure (catch the guard's Error and call projectManager.removeRepository before re-throwing).

A05 — Security Misconfiguration / Information Disclosure (Medium, CWE-209): repository-orchestrator.ts lines 112-114 — the Security check failed error message includes both the full resolved clone path (resolvedDest) and the full resolved projectsFolder path. If this Error propagates unfiltered to an API response layer, it discloses absolute filesystem paths to the caller, potentially aiding further attacks. Remediation: strip or redact the absolute path values from user-facing error messages; retain them only in server-side logs. Example safe message: 'Security check failed: clone destination is outside the allowed projects folder.'

A09 — Security Logging & Monitoring (Low): Neither the addRepositoryToProject() guard (lines 110-115) nor the removeRepositoryFromProject() guard (lines 169-174) emit a log entry when a traversal attempt is detected. Path-traversal attempts are security events that should be recorded in an audit trail (file, structured log, or monitoring hook) so operators can detect patterns of abuse. Remediation: add a structured log call (e.g., logger.warn or console.error with a structured payload) before throwing, recording the offending repositoryId and the computed resolvedDest.

A03/A10 — Info only (pre-existing, out of scope): repo.Url is passed directly to cloneRepository() without URL-scheme validation at the orchestrator level. Crafted git URLs (e.g., ext::, file://, or --upload-pack= injection) could enable git-transport-layer SSRF or command injection if not validated at registration time. This surface pre-dates this WP and is not introduced by the current change. Recommend a separate ticket to enforce an allow-list of accepted URL schemes (https://, ssh://, git://, file:// for local-only deployments) at the RepositoryManager.add() layer.
